thread:
Alex Kim: Quick check — PartnerInc wants to run healthchecks against our internal /health endpoint over their Interface VPC Endpoint (they gave vpce-0abc123). They also sent a CIDR 10.50.240.0/28 but said traffic will come via the VPCE.
Maria Chen: If it's an AWS interface VPCE, traffic can look like it comes from the endpoint ENIs in our subnet (not necessarily the partner's original IP). So allowing the raw CIDR might be incorrect.
Samir Patel: Short answer: don't open a broad CIDR. Options: 1) have them use a dedicated VPCE + provide the endpoint ID and its security group so we can reference it; 2) put healthcheck behind an ALB and require client certs/mTLS; 3) if neither, a timeboxed CIDR allowlist with an expiry and monitoring.
Maria Chen: You can't reference a security group in another account directly, but you can reference the VPCE's ENI SG if they share it with us (or they create a dedicated endpoint in our account). Also consider an endpoint policy to limit actions.
Samir Patel: Example SG change we can propose (if they supply endpoint SG):
```
# allow from partner VPCE security group (our account's sg that the endpoint uses)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-service-0123 --protocol tcp --port 8080 --source-group sg-vpce-89ab
```
If they only give CIDR and insist, require a short TTL + ticket + CIDR proof.
Taylor Nguyen: Security notes: any permanent inbound change needs a PR + sec-review. For temporary CIDRs we require: justification, owner, expiry date, and alerting on anomalous traffic. For VPC Flow Logs: we will not persist raw partner private IPs in analytics; we'll apply a redaction rule and tag entries as `partnerinc_redacted` before exporting. I'll take ownership of the redaction rule.
Alex Kim: @Taylor thanks — we'll do a PR. Partner asked about our flow logs retention — can we share the redaction approach with them?
Taylor Nguyen: Share high‑level only (we don't disclose raw logs). Tell them we retain metadata and masked identifiers, and can provide connection counts as proof.
ops-bot: Change checklist: sec-review required, audit-log enabled, endpoint policy reviewed, TTL on any CIDR allowlist, monitoring alerts set.
Alex Kim: Action items: 1) ask partner for vpce id + endpoint SG or request they create VPCE in our account. 2) if they can't, propose ALB+mTLS. 3) I'll open the PR with the SG change and set expiry to 2024-12-01.
Maria Chen: LGTM. Ping me on the PR for a quick config review.
Samir Patel: I'll add an automated alert on the service to catch any unexpected inbound peaks during the allowlist window.
Alex Kim: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
